fact: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
detail: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once, but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.
payoff: So on Venus, one sunrise-to-sunrise day lasts about two Venus years.

detail: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, while the third pumps blood around the rest of the body.
payoff: And when an octopus swims, its main body heart actually stops beating.

fact: A lightning bolt can heat the air around it hotter than the surface of the Sun.
detail: The lightning channel can reach roughly 30,000 kelvin for a tiny fraction of a second.
payoff: That sudden heating makes the air expand explosively, creating thunder.

fact: One solar day on Mercury lasts longer than a Mercury year.
detail: Mercury takes about 88 Earth days to orbit the Sun, but about 176 Earth days to go from sunrise to sunrise.
payoff: So Mercury gets one complete day in about two of its own years.

fact: Crows can remember individual human faces.
detail: Research shows crows can recognize specific people and remember faces associated with danger.
payoff: So if a crow decides it does not like you, it may remember you.

fact: There are lake-like pools of extremely salty water on the ocean floor.
detail: Dense brine can collect in deep seafloor depressions and form a visible boundary with normal seawater.
payoff: They can look like actual underwater lakes, complete with a shoreline.
